narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA designs accelerated computing platforms — GPUs, CPUs, networking and software — sold as systems and components through two segments, Compute & Networking and Graphics. Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue (193.7bn), Gaming 7.4% (16.0bn), Professional Visualization 1.5% (3.2bn), Automotive 1.1% (2.3bn) and OEM & Other 0.3% (619.0mn). Customers are hyperscalers, AI clouds, enterprises, sovereigns and OEMs; Hyperscale was about 50% of Data Center revenue in Q1 FY2027, the rest diversified across AI clouds, industrial, enterprise and sovereign buyers. The United States was 69.3% of FY2026 revenue, Taiwan 19.6% and Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1%.

Its edge is a one-year product cadence (Blackwell, then Rubin) and a dominant ~80% share of AI accelerators; AMD, Broadcom and Marvell are the closest competitors, and Taiwan Semiconductor manufactures its advanced chips. Management guides the next quarter without assuming any China data centre compute.
narrative.financial_analysis: 1H FY2027 revenue rose 95.8% to 177,837mn, gross margin reached 75.0% from 66.6% and operating profit grew 134.2% to 117,270mn; the quarter alone grew 105.9% to 96,221mn. Our forecast has revenue of 411,794mn in FY2027 (+90.7%, in line with consensus), 700,049mn in FY2028 (+70.0%, slightly above consensus on management's August ~70% view) and 947,167mn in FY2029 (+35.3%). Gross margin blends the 74.0% Q3 guide with a Q4 dip to 71–72%; tax is 16.5%. Over five years margins and ROIC expanded sharply, the balance sheet held net cash of 23,220mn at 26 Jul 2026, and the FY2026 accruals ratio was +10.9%.
narrative.valuation_overview: The rating is a probability-weighted DCF: bear USD 77.97 (25%), base USD 200.97 (55%) and bull USD 307.60 (20%) give USD 191.54 on an 11.9% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth. The model's mechanical DCF gives USD 208.98; the largest step in the bridge is our 41.0% FCF margin against the model's 43.3%, worth about USD 10 per share, because receivables and inventory absorb cash. Peer multiples imply far more (USD 303.09) and sit outside the rating. The reverse DCF shows the price needs 37.1% growth a year for five years against our 42.0%; the Monte Carlo median is USD 206.08 with 71% of draws above the price, and today's 34.5x P/E on last year's EPS is the 4th percentile of its history. Buy needs bull odds of 23%.
narrative.competitive_analysis: NVIDIA's latest-quarter revenue grew 105.9% against a peer median of 40.6%, with a 65.2% operating margin versus 21.0% and ROE of 117.2% against 30.4%; only Broadcom is close on growth and margin. On valuation it diverges: 10.6x forward earnings against a peer median of 19.0x and 20.1x EV/EBITDA against 39.5x, while the premium is on book (17.8x against 9.8x). Its edge is a one-year product cadence (Blackwell, then Rubin) and a dominant ~80% share of AI accelerators; AMD, Broadcom and Marvell are the closest competitors.
narrative.news_summary: News since late October has been dominated by governance. Press reports say CEO Jensen Huang admitted an extramarital affair on 8 November 2026 and that the board opened an independent probe into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation; the shares closed down 5.5% that day. BofA sees no evidence of proven business damage but flags governance uncertainty, and the DOJ has asked about the Hugging Face deal. Demand signals stayed positive, with Hive lining up $129 million for Nvidia chips, while state data-centre moratorium pledges and tighter China export rules cloud the outlook.
narrative.report_summary: On 26 August 2026 management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0 billion ±2%, gross margin of 74.0% ±50bp and GAAP opex of about $9.2 billion, assuming no China data centre compute; press reports on 9 November put Q4 gross margin at 71–72% and cited management's August view of roughly 70% FY2028 growth. Corporate events: $25.0 billion of senior notes issued, a definitive agreement on 2 September 2026 to acquire Hugging Face for about $11.9 billion, $105 billion of residual value guarantees on the PORTS-Pike leases for OpenAI, and $39.0bn of buybacks plus $6,290mn of dividends in the six months. Press reports describe midterm wins for candidates pledging data-centre moratoria and tighter China export rules. The 10-K flags competition, supply lead times, third-party manufacturing and geopolitics; the 10-Q adds forward-looking caution.

steps.business: NVIDIA designs chips that power artificial intelligence. Data Center is 89.7% of revenue, so one market drives the story. The United States is 69.3% of sales. Check next how much comes from a few huge cloud customers, because their spending plans steer NVIDIA.
steps.growth: Read the latest figures first. The latest quarter grew 105.9% from a year earlier, faster than the 95.8% for the half year, so growth is speeding up. The peer median is +40.6%. Warning sign: the fiscal 2027 forecast (+90.7%) is still very high, so check the next results on 17 November 2026.
steps.profit: Profit margins are very high: operating margin is 60.4% for FY2026. But cash is lagging. Cash conversion (cash received compared with profit booked) was 0.63x in the first half of FY2027, against 0.86x for the full year FY2026. Also, investment gains of USD 23.7bn sit below operating profit and are not cash. Use operating profit for the trend.
steps.safety: NVIDIA holds more cash than debt. At 26 Jul 2026 net cash was USD 23,220mn, lower than USD 41,202mn at FY2026 year-end. The company issued USD 25.0bn of new notes in the latest quarter. Check next the USD 108.5bn of guarantees and the commitments, which are promises to pay that are not yet on the balance sheet.
steps.cheap: On trailing earnings (the last twelve months), the P/E (price compared with profit per share) is 21.4x against a peer median of 46.6x. That looks cheap. But the price-to-book ratio (price against the owners' money in the books) is a premium at 17.8x. Do not mix trailing and forward measures. Trailing profit is flattered by investment gains.
steps.worth: Our probability-weighted fair value is USD 191.54, which is 13.4% above the price of USD 168.89. That is inside the Hold band, so the rating is Hold. Confidence is low because our scenarios range widely, from 77.97 to 307.60. The price implies 37.1% growth a year, less than our base case. The rating would turn to Buy if the bull case's weight rose from 20% to 23%.
steps.others: 31 brokers cover the stock, and the median target is USD 319.00. Our value is below all 31 dated targets. Brokers are often positive, and 7 targets are over 90 days old. Ask what growth, margins and risk each target assumes. Our bear case gives 25% weight to funding caution, which is the main reason for our gap.
steps.wrong: The share price fell 14.9% over one year while the S&P 500 (a broad US stock index) rose 10.1%. Its largest fall in the past year was -29.4% (a peak-to-trough drawdown, not a return); over three years the largest peak-to-trough fall was -37.0%. Risks include China export rules, an independent board probe into CEO Jensen Huang, and customers paying more slowly. Check the results on 17 November 2026.

narrative.brief:
ANALYST BRIEF (the lead analyst's view, decided before writing: build the tagline, thesis, risks, valuation and rating text on it; every figure in it is from `facts`, `news` or `filings`):
- Central question: Does FY2028 revenue growth of about 70% hold as customer financing and cash conversion stretch, enough to justify a price that implies only 37.1% growth?
- Our answer: Yes, mostly: Hold at fair value USD 191.54. Q3 is guided to $108.0 billion and supply commitments are $279 billion. But DSO rose to 60 days, 1H cash conversion was 0.63x and guarantees reach USD 108.5bn, so we weight a 25% bear case.
- What the price implies: At USD 168.89 the price implies 37.1% revenue growth a year for 5 years; our base case grows 42.0%. Forward P/E is 10.6x against a peer median of 19.0x. The market is pricing less growth than we expect, but it also discounts governance and financing risk.
- Pillar 1: Demand is visible through the guided period and the price discounts less than we forecast. Evidence: 1H FY2027 revenue 177,837mn (+95.8%); Q3 guide $108.0 billion ±2%; commitments $279 billion; reverse DCF implies +37.1% vs our +42.0%.. Breaks if: Q3 results or Q4 guidance miss the $108.0 billion guide, or FY2028 growth falls well below management's ~70% view..
- Pillar 2: Cash conversion and customer financing are the weak link in the quality of growth. Evidence: 1H operating cash flow / net profit 0.63x (0.95x a year earlier); DSO 60 days vs 45; guarantees USD 108.5bn; investment gains 23,707mn.. Breaks if: DSO keeps rising or OpenAI/PORTS-Pike lease payments slip so guarantees are called..
- Pillar 3: CEO and policy overhang justifies Hold despite the cheap multiple. Evidence: Shares are 29.4% below the October record; board probe into Huang; Democrats won both chambers in the midterms and the state data-center moratorium pledges threaten planned capacity.. Breaks if: The probe clears with no business impact and policy risk eases, lifting the bull case odds from 20% to 23%..
- Beyond our forecast years: Bull: the $500bn financing platforms and PORTS-Pike upgrade cycles sustain growth beyond the FY2029 fade to +35.3%. Bear: AI funding turns cautious, moratoria bite, customers stretch, growth falls to -4.7% and the FCF margin settles at 34.0%.
- Revenue and profit quality: Investment gains of 23,707mn are about 20% of 1H net profit and are not cash; net profit grew +161.1% vs operating profit +134.2%. Cash conversion was 0.63x vs 0.95x. DSO rose to 60 days. Accruals ratio +10.9% in FY2026. Guarantees are USD 108.5bn.
- Governance: Press reports say Jensen Huang admitted an affair on 8 November 2026, and the board has launched an independent probe into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. BofA sees no proven business damage. What is proven is unknown. Ives puts removal odds at about 15%.
- Where we differ from the brokers: Our USD 191.54 is below all 31 dated broker targets (lowest USD 200.00; median USD 319.00). We weight a 25% bear case and hold FCF margin at 41.0%, below the model's 43.3%, because receivables and inventory absorb cash. Brokers appear to extrapolate growth.
- What to watch: 17 November results: guide $108.0 billion ±2%, our FY2027 revenue 411,794mn. Decisive is Q4 guidance and gross margin (the press reports 71-72%) plus DSO. 18 November: congressional briefing request to Huang. Options price ±10.3%.
- Tagline (by the lead analyst; use it as the report's tagline as written): The market prices AI financing and CEO risk as a collapse; the evidence says growth holds, with limited upside
- Thesis paragraph (by the lead analyst; use it as the thesis, changing only what a rule or `feedback` requires; a deep report adds one sentence on the debate's verdict and swing factor): The question is whether roughly 70% FY2028 growth survives stretched customer financing. We think mostly yes: Q3 is guided to $108.0 billion and commitments are $279 billion. At USD 168.89 the price implies 37.1% growth for 5 years against our 42.0%, so it is not demanding. But 1H cash conversion fell to 0.63x, DSO reached 60 days, guarantees total USD 108.5bn, and the CEO probe adds uncertainty. Our scenarios give USD 191.54 (+13.4%), a Hold with low confidence, close to the Buy line if the bull odds rose to 23%. We are below all 31 dated broker targets because of the 25% bear weight.

It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms.
